decisions.suggestion: Answered 2026-11-12: let the computer recruit. Measured in M4.4: even free workers lower its score (labour is not the limit; inputs and freight cars are). See card Q21.

decisions.title: Hide the Materials and Goods groups in the transport popup until something produces them?
decisions.context: In v1 all materials and goods show 0 / 0 in the transport popup, and the rules say some (paper, canned food, armaments) can never be shipped.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-12 (NR-027): done in M4.4; empty groups are hidden.

decisions.title: Should a Board of Trade button the engine would refuse be disabled with its reason?
decisions.context: M7 UI decision 4 kept the v1 way (press, then read "Purchase refused: over the limit."). The review asked for the M6 way: the "+" is disabled and its title says why: "No free hold this turn", "Already 4 bids this turn, the most", "None left in the warehouse", "Not enough money" (FR-248).
decisions.suggestion: Done in the review fix round (FR-248).

decisions.title: Should the computer place a standing steel and lumber bid toward you?
decisions.context: Decides FR-539 (the Steel row of the Board of Trade in a real game; M13 review ST-02 and by-eye QA check 4). Before: Valdoria never bid for steel toward you in a real game (0 of 24 sim games, and every QA game), so the Steel row never invited an offer. Nobody had answered, so the M13 close round (2026-11-17, branch claude/m13-nations, not merged) built option (b), narrowed: from turn 7 Valdoria bids for 1 steel a turn toward a Great Power a person plays, before the bids for its mills' inputs, and keeps only the upkeep reserve as its cash floor (an unanswered bid is refunded the same turn). Measured: the Steel row says "Valdoria bid for 1 last turn" on 10 to 12 of turns 3 to 20 in 24 of 24 idle games (was 0), and a player who answers sells it 7 to 10 steel in 24 of 24 games (was 1); every other M13 row still holds and the v1 tests did not move. Not checked by eye in the app.

options.label: Option (a)
options.means: A standing bid of 1 steel and 1 lumber from turn 1. The review fix round's version met FR-539 in 24 of 24 games; the close round's variant from turn 1 met the Steel row in only 11 of 24 and had 2 regiments disbanded for want of pay. It changes one M12 continent test in tests/engine/scriptedScore.test.ts (seed 1, turn 6), which M13 may not re-record without your answer (FR-498).

options.label: Option (b), built
options.means: The standing bid from turn 7, after that test's turns. As built: steel only (with lumber too, Valdoria went to war with Testland in 21 of 24 both-computer games instead of 10), and only toward a nation a person plays. The Lumber row already lights once you answer Valdoria's lumber bid (FR-541).

options.label: Option (c)
options.means: No standing bid: the Steel row lights only when Valdoria has a free hold, which in a real game is almost never (0 of 24 games, and every QA game). FR-539 would open again.

decisions.suggestion: Option (b) as built (it was option (a) before the close round; (b) meets FR-539 without changing the M12 test).
decisions.objection: Valdoria spends 1 of its 4 holds a turn from turn 7 on a bid only a trading player answers (refunded otherwise). The race for Arvelia moves in the games where the computer plays both nations: Valdoria takes it first in 14 of 24 (was 6), Testland declares war on Valdoria in 7 of 24 (was 1), and Testland's lowest final score falls from 1117 to 854 (one game). Three continent test files were re-recorded with old and new numbers (FR-499).

decisions.title: Should a Great Power's bid be served before the minors' demand?
decisions.context: Decides how the trade phase shares Valdoria's goods (FR-186, FR-492, FR-493 (b)). In the QA games none of 69 bids of the player for Valdoria's clothing or furniture filled: the minors' demand takes Valdoria's 1 to 2 a turn first (settlement step 2). For the same reason a timber offer to Valdoria never sells (the minors fill its timber bid first, step 1).

options.label: Option (a), suggested
options.means: Keep the order until M14; the Board already says a bid is refunded.

options.label: Option (b)
options.means: Serve a Great Power's bid for goods in step 2, together with the minors, in id order. Moves every "partners" pin.

options.label: Option (c)
options.means: The computer keeps a share of its goods for the other Great Power's bid of last turn.

decisions.suggestion: Option (a) until M14.
decisions.objection: The Board invites bids that never pay.

decisions.title: After you accept the computer's peace, may it declare war on you again?
decisions.context: Decides FR-488's 10-turn pause after a peace (by-eye QA track A). An idle player who accepts the first peace (turn 27) is attacked again on turn 37 and loses a second province by turn 40. The spec's QA check 8 asks only for 10 quiet turns.

options.label: Option (a)
options.means: As built: a new war 10 turns after any peace.

options.label: Option (b)
options.means: No new war on a player who accepted its peace.

options.label: Option (c), suggested
options.means: A longer pause after an accepted peace, for example 20 turns.

decisions.suggestion: Option (c).
decisions.objection: With (a) a player who accepts peace is punished like one who refuses it; with (b) the computer has nothing to do after its first war.

decisions.title: What should change so a minor can vote for the computer at the turn-30 Council?
decisions.context: Decides FR-542, which replaces FR-490's turn-30 threshold (M13 close round, 2026-11-17). FR-490 asked for a minor's vote for Valdoria at the turn-30 meeting in 18 of 24 idle games. With the embassy, the pact and the grants it gets 0 of 24 at turn 30 and 18 of 24 at turn 40: the best free minor stands at 37 to 48 points at turn 30 and a vote needs 50. Valdoria can afford the $5,000 embassy from about turn 23, the turn it goes to war with you, and that war keeps its cash at the upkeep of every turn left, so it pays almost no grant before turn 30. 36 rule sets were measured (.gate/m13/close/grants-notes.md).

options.label: Option (a), suggested
options.means: Keep FR-542 as built: the computer's minor votes come at the turn-40 meeting (18 of 24), not at turn 30 (0 of 24).

options.label: Option (b)
options.means: A minor votes for a nominee from 40 relation points instead of 50 (a remake number, card Q52): 23 of 24 at turn 30 and 24 of 24 at turn 40 with FR-542 (5 of 24 at turn 30 without it). Your votes change too, and every Council test moves.

options.label: Option (c)
options.means: The computer waits with its war on you until after the turn-30 meeting: with a wait of 8 turns, 0 of 24 at turn 30 and 39 to 101 regiments disbanded for want of pay, so it needs a new cash rule first.

options.label: Option (d)
options.means: A cheaper embassy, for example $2,000 (the game keeps Imp1's $5,000): not measured.

decisions.suggestion: Option (a) for M13; option (b) if the turn-30 vote matters, as a Council rule for both sides.
decisions.objection: With (a) you see no minor vote for the computer at turn 30, as in the by-eye QA, and the M13 spec moves its promise to turn 40; with (b) a minor is easier to win for you too, and the Council can end the game earlier.
decisions.needed: Before the M13 pull request is merged: FR-490's turn-30 threshold was the spec's, and FR-542 replaces it with the measured ceiling.

decisions.title: Ship preparation only for computer nations
decisions.context: Advance hull preparation reserves lumber and fabric that could fund other investment. The M14 diplomat uses the shared economic planner for a human-controlled nation.
decisions.ruling: Nathan, 2026-11-20. Only a computer-controlled nation prepares future hull materials. The normal ship order remains available when either controller has the materials and meets the fleet-use conditions.
decisions.objection: With identical stocks the human invested in industry and the computer reserved the hull. The original diplomat won 15/24 under FR-545 (Q142). The idle fleet qualified in 24/24 for FR-516.

decisions.title: When can a lawful Council purchase earn a minor vote?
decisions.context: Valdoria earned a voluntary turn-40 vote in 21/24 idle games with the spending bypass and 13/24 after the supplier, cash reserve and mill demand checks.
decisions.ruling: Nathan, 2026-11-20, allowed one extra eligible turn before the final Council window under FR-245. On 2026-11-21 you accepted FR-546 in place of FR-542 (ii): at least one free minor must vote voluntarily for the computer at the turn-40 Council in at least 13 of 24 idle games. FR-542 (i) still requires the embassy and pact in at least 18 of 24.
decisions.objection: Seven seeds used the extra turn. Both lawful windows earned the vote in the same 13 games, below the previous 18/24 target. Compare the computer's final purchases and earned votes with the original game.

decisions.title: How often must the peaceful diplomat win with the M15 computer fleet?
decisions.context: Before FR-516 added the computer fleet, the M14 diplomat won all 24 games. With computer-only advance ship preparation, the same diplomat wins 15. FR-509 required 18.
decisions.ruling: Nathan, 2026-11-21. You accepted FR-545 in place of FR-509's diplomat threshold. The diplomat must win a Council by turn 40 without declaring war in at least 15 of 24 games.
decisions.objection: Nine previously winning games now end in defeat. Compare a peaceful player's ability to win the Council against a growing computer fleet in the original game.

decisions.title: When should the computer buy a technology?
decisions.context: The parked buyer-only branch proposes FR-547. It buys at most one affordable invention per turn when a recruit, ship or collected resource project will use it within three turns. The main game has no computer technology buyer.
decisions.suggestion: Record the availability, affordability, purchase and first use of inventions in the original game before tuning the buyer.
decisions.objection: The branch bought Streamlined Hulls on turn 3 and ordered a Clipper on turn 6. Its spending weakened minor votes and province captures.

decisions.title: How much water can a squadron cross in one turn?
decisions.context: The small fixed map has ocean hexes and coastal provinces, but no historical sea-zone boundaries. Rail deployment also needs a land/sea boundary.

options.label: Use province approaches
options.means: A reachable coast takes one sail Order, followed by a separate station turn. Domestic rail stays on the same landmass. A stationed fleet can also reinforce a friendly shore within its support limit.

options.label: Map several sea zones
options.means: Ships travel by their printed speed across a new zone map. The crossing may take more turns.

decisions.suggestion: Use province approaches for the first playable crossing.
decisions.objection: Short and long voyages take the same time, and holding one approach can close several ports in that province. The original’s limit for follow-up reinforcements is uncertain.
decisions.ruling: approved by owner 2026-11-22. A reachable coast takes one sail Order, followed by a separate station turn. Domestic rail stays on the same landmass. A stationed fleet can also reinforce a friendly shore within its support limit.

decisions.title: What happens when an enemy fleet intercepts a landing?
decisions.context: The rules describe automatic interception and possible losses. They give ship stats but no engagement odds or drowning rate.

options.label: Resolve by total firepower
options.means: The weaker squadron returns intact. Equal forces stay, block the landing and leave the port contested.

options.label: Hold every opposed landing
options.means: Both sides stay until a fleet withdraws. Fleet strength has no effect on that engagement.

decisions.suggestion: Use total firepower and report the strengths, retreat or tie.
decisions.objection: A large fleet of weak ships can win on total guns alone, ignoring range and armour. No hull or troop can be lost at sea.
decisions.ruling: Revised by the owner 2026-11-22 and implemented locally. FR-552 resolves three seeded rounds with hull damage, losses and berth repair. FR-560 orders allied attacks by total ARMS, stopping after capture.

decisions.title: When should the computer spend on warships?
decisions.context: M15 buys merchant holds from observed cargo use. Previous speculative spending weakened Council votes and the one-province campaign. The original naval budget and invasion timing are unknown.

options.label: Respond to a visible threat
options.means: Use existing hulls or fund one Frigate after a hostile squadron is seen off one of the computer’s ports.

options.label: Prepare an offensive fleet
options.means: Divert stocks before a threat to seek island wars. This also changes the opening army and diplomacy.

decisions.suggestion: Respond to a visible threat. Measure offensive opportunities before choosing a purchase or invasion policy.
decisions.objection: A quiet player can take an island minor without a rival naval race, and a reactive build may arrive too late to save a port.
decisions.ruling: approved by owner 2026-11-22. Use existing hulls or fund one Frigate after a hostile squadron is seen off one of the computer’s ports.

history.says: Requirements exist, but "tested" means less than it sounds: 46 requirement rows still carry an open clarification, 55 of 75 decision cards are open, and 11 rule topics of the original were never given a milestone.

history.title: World and seams: provinces, 4 minor nations
history.says: Twelve provinces and 4 minors show as claimed. Three of the four minors are islands that cannot be reached, there is one map only, and each minor is far weaker than in the original.

history.title: Diplomacy: overtures, nine relation levels
history.says: Consulate, embassy, pact, grants, war and peace all work in the app. A subsidy is shown as free, the screen explains nothing, an alliance is only a flag, and the Accept Offer dialog cannot be reached in normal play.

history.title: Nation-to-nation trade: Bids and Offers, Deal Book
history.says: Human and computer trade work. Trade is capped at 4 units a turn, trade with the other Great Power never happens, 10 of 17 rows can never trade, and the older World market dialog cannot be opened.

history.title: Armies: Armoury, regiments, upkeep, Army screen
history.says: Recruiting and marching work in the app. Horses cannot be replenished, forts are never drawn, Move and Range change nothing, and a $100 shortfall disbands the whole army without saying so.

history.title: War: attack screen, battles, taking provinces, computer at war
history.says: War works against Arvelia only. The other three minors are impossible, the computer starts a war in a third of games and never attacks or defends, and the game still offers war on islands.

history.title: Council of Governors vote
history.says: The Council screen and countdown work. "More than two thirds wins" never happens in any simulated game (no game ended by Council in 376 meetings), and the nominee text contradicts the votes.

history.title: Ink-and-wash restyle: the art pack across the game
history.says: The pack shows everywhere and 7 dialogs fit at 5 window sizes. At the audit the progress data still said "in review", one cursor could never appear, depot and port marks were tiny, the credits omitted the art pack, and phone width broke. M11 was merged as PR 30 (main 3d819d6).

findings.title: The computer nation campaigns in only a third of the games; in the others it stalls at 2 of 3 Cuirassiers with no trained worker left
When invaded, the computer never recruits: the 'garrison recruits Regulars' rule can never run, and it loses 3 of its 4 provinces in 3 turns
The computer builds mills it cannot staff and never recruits workers; its workforce shrinks from 7 to 4 or 5
The computer never deals with, proposes to or attacks the other Great Power, so the human is never approached
A Council of Governors vote can never be won peacefully: the best possible is 8 votes of the 9 needed, so no game ended by Council in 376 meetings
The upkeep warning says cash is enough, then End Turn disbands regiments because a subsidised bid costs more than its reserve
Only Arvelia can ever be attacked: Sundmark, Lorran and Pellis border no province, so the 'war on minors' and the colonies row cover one minor, for one Great Power
At war with the player the computer nation does nothing: no recruit, no march, no attack, hoards 2 armaments (carried item FR-213 confirmed in the running game)
The computer's war on minors (FR-274) starts in only 19% of random games; in 81% it stalls at 2 Cuirassiers with up to $15,000 idle
The computer never attacks the player and never defends, so a conquest win on turn 13 needs only 9 regiments
Three of the four minor nations (Sundmark, Lorran, Pellis) can never be attacked: no ships, no landing
The game lets the player declare war on an island minor that can never be attacked, with no warning
Deal Book shows 'Trade net -$100' with 'No deals last turn': the army upkeep hides inside Trade net
Attack and Battle screens hide regiments beyond about 8 per side behind an unmarked inner scroll area
Move and Range are printed on the Armoury cards but change nothing (melee firepower is stored and unused); Light Artillery and Skirmishers are dominated units
Horses (needed by Hussars, Cuirassiers, Light Artillery) have no source: the 4 start horses are all a player ever gets
Forts are never drawn on the map (also not the one the Engineer builds for $5,000) and only level 1 exists; the Attack screen is the only place that shows one
No rail or transport move for armies: one bordering province per turn, so the start army needs 2 turns to reach Arvelia
Medals, generals, experience and army rewards from the rules are not in the game
A $100 upkeep shortfall disbands the whole army, and the warning does not say so
Cancelling an attack needs one click per regiment; there is no 'Cancel attack' for the whole force
Clicking an enemy tile that the selected army does not border does nothing and silently drops the selection
The HUD never says the player is at war; war state is only in the Diplomacy tabs
Valdoria asks for peace every 3 turns from the first turn of war, before any battle; the offer, the Battle screen and the Council dialog can stack at turn start
Conquest is by far the cheapest way to score: taking Arvelia on turn 2 adds +109 points (45% of the start score) with no development work
Requirements and journal call the scripted war 'tested' and 'done' while it only holds on four pinned seeds
A Council victory cannot be reached by diplomacy; it always needs a war that takes land from Valdoria
The computer nation never attacks or counter-attacks; it lets itself lose 3 of its 4 provinces
The computer starts a war in only a third of games, never against a Great Power, and never offers an alliance or a pact
A subsidy is shown as "free" but silently cuts all income from that minor, down to $0 at 100%
Alliance, pact and embassy do nothing beyond a chip and a few relation points
The Diplomacy screen never says what an overture does or what thresholds matter
The player cannot see what decides the minors' votes: relation points are hidden and the rival's standing with the minors is invisible
"1st nominee / 2nd nominee" and the news line contradict the vote counts
Accept Offer opens on top of the Battle screen (and the Council screen): two modal dialogs at once, the first half hidden
When the computer wins the Council the screen still says "Valdoria Wins!" in the same green and the game-over screen has no defeat wording
The Diplomacy dialog is unusable below about 500 px width: the details pane shrinks to 34 px
Trade policy accepts a no-op and a contradiction: "Set policy" with nothing changed is an order, and Subsidy 100% together with Boycott is allowed
A game cannot be saved; a page reload throws away a 40-turn game
The last Council is not a forced vote, so the turn-40 meeting almost never decides the game
No peaceful way to use a high relation: Join the Empire, pact intervention and colony boycott are not built, so levels 7 to 9 are only a vote
The computer's peace offer returns every 3 turns with no context and needs a click each time
Conquering a minor sets the relation to dark green with no news line
Peace repairs nothing: after "Peace made with Lorran" the relation stays at war level and all treaties must be bought again
Closing an Accept Offer with the x cannot be undone: the offer is gone from every screen for the turn
Diplomacy shows nothing about the other country's strength, so war and peace are chosen blind
No total of promised (locked) grants on the Diplomacy screen
Transport sliders do not limit anything: spare capacity is filled automatically, so "Allocated 0 / Remaining 15" still ships everything
An engineer cannot lay the last rail section into the capital by clicking it: the click silently becomes a plain move and the turn is lost

With an engineer selected the capital shows the "build fort" cursor, but the click is refused ("not a valid site"); the engineer cursor also shows "build" on every own tile although a click only moves
The tile panel builds a $5,000 fort on any tile with one click, shows no price or confirmation, and the finished fort is not visible anywhere
The tile panel offers buttons that always fail: "Develop farmer" on a coal hill (enabled), "Construct Port" inland, "Construct Depot" beside a depot or the capital; the refusal gives no reason
The Construction Options dialog shows no price, no duration and offers "Build Depot" where it is always refused
After a plain move the civilian stays selected, so every later click on another tile (just to look at it) shows "Move refused: the worker already moved this turn."
Clicking another civilian while one is selected moves the selected one next to it instead of switching the selection; there is no other way to deselect
Cancel: the confirm box does not say if money comes back, a job cancelled on a later turn silently loses its price, and a move plus job needs two Cancel clicks
One click on a tile can spend $1,000 to $5,000 (develop level 2 or 3) with no price shown and no confirmation
A new player gets no hint what to do: no goal text, no tutorial, no first-step prompt, hidden "n" shortcut
No save or load: reloading or closing the tab destroys the game
Civilians can never be built (no University) and technology cannot be bought: the start seven civilians are all you ever have
Town development (free materials and goods from connected towns, "a large free income" in rules 04) does not exist
The player cannot see which tiles a depot collects: tile panel and transport popup show no network state, yield or coverage
Once a tile is selected the news shows 3 lines (6 at 1080p) of about 12-20, the HUD must be scrolled, and a tile cannot be deselected
Capital dialog is cut off at 1280x720 and 1366x768: the Clothing factory card and the Transport footer need an inner scroll
A "Debug" box with tile coordinates and the game seed shows in the player HUD
Warehouse lists Canned Food, Paper and Fuel under "Materials"; a job row in the tile panel wraps its text ("Forestry to level" / "2" / Cancel)
The Board of Trade lets you offer more units than the minor buyers take; the surplus wastes a cargo hold
Upkeep warning wording contradicts itself: "$50 is due ... and $16 will be left"
Rules 04 says cotton and wool share one transport slider and the popup shows demand lines; the app has separate Cotton and Wool sliders and no demand display
The score formula punishes investment: ordering a job lowers the score at once, and level 3 development costs 50 points for +10
A rail click onto a tile that already has a job silently becomes a plain move: no rail, no message, no cursor
Goods shipped this turn arrive after production, so they are used one turn later; nothing in the transport popup or capital says so
Three of the four minor nations can never be attacked or taken, but the game offers war on them
The Council of Governors vote can practically never end a game; every simulated game ends on turn 40
There is no technology system; the Technology button is disabled and the Oil Refinery and Fuel can never be reached
Milestone M4.4 is titled "Recruiting AI" but the computer never recruits workers
docs/report/roadmap.json contradicts itself about what is done
The status "tested" in requirements.md does not mean what a reader expects
The tile panel offers Construct Depot, Port and Fort on the capital, where all three are invalid; the refusal shows far away
FR-330 says five cursors from the pack; the "build rail" cursor can never appear
Two "tested" requirements contradict each other: NR-016 (orders take effect at End Turn) and FR-021 (orders take effect when submitted)
The Accept Offer dialog and the alliance flow cannot happen in normal play and have no browser test
docs/rules "CODE MISMATCH" lines are stale, and the M2 goal to close them was never finished
Dead code: a no-op turn phase, 3 orphan files and about 10 unused exports remain
Repository hygiene: a third-party manual, 13 MB of screenshots, one-off probes, template files and demo pages are tracked or served
Three lint warnings (0 errors, tsc clean)
A few tests cannot fail or only print numbers
Trade is narrow: 4 units a turn for the whole game, and only 3 finished goods have buyers
ARCHITECTURE.md and rules/01 still describe fixtures and a difficulty setting that do not exist in play
Trade is capped at 4 units a turn for the whole game: no merchant ships, no Shipyard, holds never grow
Trade with the other Great Power (Valdoria) never happens; the Board invites offers that always come back unsold
Trade profit is nearly worthless in the score and cash has no use: $24,621 earned, 246 points, while idle capacity gives the computer 720 points
Trade orders are forgotten every turn, while production orders in the same Capital dialog persist
The v1 'World market' dialog (FR-073, FR-074, FR-078) cannot be reached in the app; Open Market always opens the Board of Trade
The Board shows only the base price; a subsidy changes what a deal pays and the Board does not say so (100% subsidy sells for $0)
Running out of money silently disbands regiments; no warning in Diplomacy or Board, and the rules' credit limit does not exist
When the computer conquers a trade partner the player's consulate, embassy and subsidy vanish with no news line and no refund
Ten of the 17 Board rows can never trade, and minor supply and demand never change in 40 turns
Prices are a random walk with no history or trend; buying low and selling high is luck
The favourite partner flips every turn on equal relations, against the fixed order in the rules
No guidance for the first turns of trade: nothing to sell until turn 3, and the Board does not say what to do
The computer nation trades about 1 unit a turn, builds capacity it cannot staff and scores 3.5 times the player
HUD news panel shows 3 of about 19 lines in a 60 px box with free space below it, so the turn's Sold/Bought lines are hidden
Board of Trade is unusable on a narrow screen: at 390 px wide the Bid and Offer columns are 623 px off to the side
Offered goods disappear from the Warehouse dialog at order time with no 'on offer' marker
A $10,000 grant can be given with one click and no confirmation; the cash simply leaves the game
No technology tree: 28 technologies, the purchase screen and research are missing
Resource levels 2 and 3 and the Rancher, Forester and Driller need no technology: whole development ladder open on turn 1
No University: civilians cannot be built, a nation has exactly 7 for the whole game, and there is no Developer
Merchant marine is frozen at 4 cargo holds: no Shipyard, trade is capped at 4 units per turn for the whole game
No navy or sea war: fleets are empty arrays, the interceptions phase is a TODO, and 3 of the 4 minor nations can never be reached
The world has only 6 of 14 land terrains and 7 of 13 resources: no wool, fish, horses, oil, gold or gems, no mountains, swamp, desert, tundra, rivers
One hand-drawn map for every game: no key-word or seeded map, no Great Power/minor choice, 2 Great Powers, 4 minors, 12 provinces
No Developer, overseas profits or Join the Empire: minor nations are only trading partners and conquest is the only way to a colony
Horses can never be replenished: 4 horses for the whole game cap Hussars, Cuirassiers and Light Artillery at 4 units in total, also for the computer
No save or load: reloading the page throws the game away
Game-over ranking ignores provinces, army and the Council: a nation with 1 of 12 provinces can rank first
Trade bids and offers are cleared every turn; the original keeps them
Minor nations are constant machines: fixed offers and demand, endless money, price only moves with the two Great Powers
No credit, interest or forced sale; the Deal Book is not the original ledger
No town development: provinces never grow or ship free steel, lumber, fabric and goods
Oil, fuel, Oil Refinery and Power Plant are unreachable dead code; labour can never exceed people
Transport rules not modelled: river ports and fish, blockade, depot-on-port rule, cutting a line by conquering a province downstream
The Engineer can move and start a depot, port, fort or rail in the same turn; the rules say he must rest the turn after moving
Minor nations are far weaker than in the rules: one province, 3 Minutemen, no fort
Land war is era 1 only: 9 of 27 regiments (7 recruitable), no Generals, medals, Sappers, walls, landings or rail deployment, forts level 1 only
Diplomacy leftovers: no colony boycott, no Foreign Minister auto-subsidy, no intervention, no allied defence; an alliance is only a flag, and the computer never allies or attacks the human

Many original screens have no counterpart: Offer Sheet and Foreign Minister advice, Trade Book, diplomacy map modes, strength charts and rankings, Garrison Book, Scouting Report, Task Force, reward popups, Technology, University, Shipyard
Capital dialog: the Technology button is disabled; every other advertised item works
No difficulty levels, scenarios or game options; game length fixed at 40 turns (10 years)
Prospecting always succeeds with a fixed answer; "may find nothing" and the random mineral pick never happen
Dead rows for goods nobody can make: Wool, Fish, Oil, Fuel and (after 4) Horses appear in Warehouse, Transport and Board lists
Trade School and Capitol buttons look available but fail with a message that does not name the missing good

"Everything done" is true only for a compact scope: no milestone exists for 11 rule topics of the original (technology, University, Shipyard and navy, Developer and colonies, town development, power, credit, saving, difficulty, forced Council vote, era 2-3 units)

After clicking a tile, the Tile Info, workers, job state and news are below the fold of the HUD pane; on small windows the panel is not visible at all

The Capital dialog has a permanently disabled 'Technology' button (placeholder: 'Coming in a later milestone')
No zoom, and on large screens the small map is not centred: at 1920x1080 it fills the top-left quarter and the rest is empty sea

Board of Trade: the 'Minor Nations' column (who buys and sells, and which consulate is missing) is cut off at 800x600 and below

Small text and small click targets: 10 px notes in the Board of Trade, 22x22 px stepper buttons, 21x24 px About close button
Disabled controls are drawn at 2.1 to 2.4 to 1 contrast, including the always-disabled Cancel buttons
Council dialog at 800x600 is taller than the window; focus on Close scrolls the title and picture out of view
No page landmarks, no h1 and no live region: the HUD title is an h2 and news, refusals and the food warning are not announced

Depot and port marks are tiny and an engineer standing on the tile hides them; the capital picture is mostly covered by the army marker and the civilian stack
About credits name only Game Icons; the ink-and-wash art pack that draws the map, goods, buildings and figures is not mentioned
